subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Should WebChat agent context expose gateway client identity, and if so which fields are trusted versus advisory?
rationale: The gateway already knows client ids and modes, but making them model-visible may influence native-only behavior, debugging, deep links, or privileged UX, so automation should not choose the trust semantics.

options.title: Expose Sanitized Advisory Metadata
options.body: Propagate a narrow client class such as browser, macos, ios, or android into runtime context and document it as non-authoritative for security or permission decisions.

options.title: Expose Only Attested Native Identity
options.body: Surface native/app identity only when backed by device-auth or pairing evidence, leaving browser-provided hints out of agent-visible context.

options.title: Keep Identity Internal
options.body: Leave client identity in Gateway policy/logging only and solve specific UX differences through explicit capability APIs or diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Expose Sanitized Advisory Metadata
recommendation.body: Propagate a narrow client class such as browser, macos, ios, or android into runtime context and document it as non-authoritative for security or permission decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans Gateway protocol identity, runtime prompt metadata, and security semantics already tied to steipete's history on these surfaces.
